correctness.rationale: For the normalized unit-modulus matrix with first row and column ones, singularity is (u−1)(t−1)=(v−1)(w−1). When nonzero, conjugate and divide to get ut=vw, then u+t=v+w, so the pairs coincide and two rows or columns coincide. In the zero case one factor from each side vanishes, giving a row or column equal to the first. The possible (k_R,k_C) are (0,0) at rank 3, (1,0),(0,1),(1,1) at rank 2, and (3,3) at rank 1, so the −9 overlap at rank one explains the +4 correction in the singularity indicator. A difference of gcd a has an annihilator of size a and gives Nφ(N/a)/2 unordered pairs (including the self-opposite nonzero difference, since reversing an ordered pair still changes its endpoints); (N/a)·binom(a,3) counts allowed column triples in annihilator cosets. For simultaneous pairs, N|de iff N|ab by truncated prime valuations, and there are a−2 and b−2 completions in the relevant cosets. A size-one annihilator cannot occur on either side for an admissible simultaneous pair, and a size-two annihilator contributes zero. For rank one, all row differences generate the subgroup with gcd h and a complete column triple lies in a common-annihilator coset. The incidence k|h amounts exactly to k·binom(N/k,3), which inverts to M_h on the divisor lattice. This reconstructs all three formulas, including the prime boundary P=Q=L=0. Independent exact replay at /workspace/branches/3a9629ab-ac15-450f-93ec-7b3369112b66/rank30_exact_replay.py checks every anchored pair via integer cyclotomic reduction, giving (180,15192,149464), with largest reduced coefficient magnitude 6. In a double count with anchors, each unrestricted pair has 9 anchor choices, and each anchored pair has 30² translated preimages with anchors, giving scale 100 even when some triples have stabilizers. The divisor intermediates P=919800, Q=374400, L=18000 agree. This corroborates N=30, not the all-N argument. Complex rank only, no larger minors or stability conclusion.

evidence: Caragea–Lee Theorems 1.1–1.2 fix the same indices on both sides; Theorem 1.1 gives principal invertibility at squarefree sizes, using a specialized normalized 3×3 determinant in §3. Their statements do not control nonprincipal pairs, e.g. the singular ones at squarefree N=30.

Krahmer et al. Prop. 3.6 gives existence in certain sizes and an adjacency sufficient condition. Delvaux–Van Barel's accessible article abstract targets maximal rank-deficient blocks via hierarchical subdivisions. Bonami–Ghobber's Prop. 11 gives a product-group minimum Fourier-support formula and Thm. 17 characterizes certain extremizers for distinct-prime groups.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Maximal-block constructions require incidence multiplicities and their overlaps to recover counts of smaller restrictions; the inspected prior material does not supply those. Principal and adjacent restrictions constrain indices, and extremal theorems erase the multiplicity information by taking a minimum.

evidence: At N=10 the earlier even-semiprime formula gives 1600 rank-two restrictions, agreeing with the specialized sums; at N=15 the earlier 3p result gives 300 rank-one and 13800 rank-two restrictions. These known laws do not include N=30 or cyclic orders with mixed repeated prime factors. A tensor-product Fourier identity cannot multiply arbitrary triple counts as arbitrary row and column triples need not be Cartesian products of index subsets.
The local proportional-pair criterion alone does not give the incidence law: joint pair incidences and rank-one overlap require distinct arithmetic counts and corrections.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Checked antecedents substantiate restricted cases and structural ingredients, not an automatic extension or a stronger enumerative theorem. The all-order divisor-sum census, rather than its known restrictions or primitive lemma, is the proper priority unit.

evidence: Fourier sign, normalization, separate translations and swapping rows with columns leave rank invariant. For fixed input support C and prescribed output zeros R, rank r means an allowed coefficient nullspace of dimension 3−r; requiring every coefficient nonzero is an extra condition, and optimizing the number of zeros over C is a different statistic.

Earlier cf7d7124f263 gives the sharp maximum 2N/q_N off the exact three-point support locus, not the number of pairs with nullity 0, 1 or 2. Earlier a8ba65401394 prescribes equal-magnitude coefficients and stratifies their zero sets.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Rank multiplicities would be equivalent to a joint prescribed-zero-set nullspace dimension distribution for all ordered pairs of arbitrary triples. Neither exact three-point uncertainty nor a binary singularity or full-spark existence criterion records that distribution.

value.rationale: The rank is exactly the dimension of the observed signal subspace for a specified three-point cyclic sampling and three selected frequencies. Counting separately one- and two-dimensional deficiencies, including their overlap, is stronger than showing a singular minor exists, classifying extremal supports, or tabulating a few moduli. The formulas replace all-triple enumeration at every cyclic order with integer divisor sums and explicitly pass beyond prime powers and products of two primes. This is a useful exact reference for third-order degeneracy, not a guarantee of good conditioning.
